Spilled alcohol on my Asus Vivobook 15 and took it to Gauhar within 12 hours to clean the spillage. Had followed all first aid protocol of liquid spillage (switch it off, keep the laptop inverted in a sealed plastic box with silica gel, drained all excess liquid etc). Before the cleaning Gauhar switched on the laptop to verify that it was alive. Everything worked properly before he started working on it. However after an hour long isopropyl bath of all the internal components and scrubbing with a toothbrush by his assistant (which I think was not required as there was no dust at all) , once he re-assembled the laptop, the display wouldn't turn on. The laptop was with him for over 6 days and eventually he declared a motherboard problem and handed back to me in a worse condition than when I had brought it in.

I took it to a friend's father who owns an IT store and after a few days of trying to fix it, he eventually called it a lost cause and confirmed that the damage was due to manhandling of the motherboard (most likely due to very harsh scrubbing, which damaged a few components on the board).

To be honest, Gauhar himself seems like a genuine fellow, but his business is only as good as his staff, and the kid who was scrubbing my motherboard screwed it up big time. Had Gauhar paid attention to what his team was doing, I would still have my laptop in working condition. After realising his team messed up, it seemed he tired his best to fix it, but the story ends in disappointment.

When I came back to collect my dead laptop, the two rubber pads underneath the laptop were missing and the screws of the back panel weren't screwed in properly.

Gauhar kept blaming the motherboard damage on the liquid spill and defended and justified himself, dispite confirming that the laptop was fully functional before he and his team started working on it. The laptop went dead AFTER the cleaning. The other technicians confirmed the motherboard was physically damaged.

Few points - please NEVER allow anyone to douse your motherboard in isopropyl and scrub it with a toothbrush, no matter what they say. Even if its liquid damaged, do spot-cleaning (using isopropyl on a earbud) to remove the liquid from the IC. Make sure the isopropyl that is being used for spot-cleaning is atleast 90% concentration of alcohol. I trusted Gauhar and his incompetent team, and it cost me my laptop.

I don't think I can ever recommend PC Clinic to anyone for any risky work. Need to install a new ram or hdd, sure they can handle it. Anything even mildly challenging, I would not recommend. I wouldn't ever trust them with my machine.

Thankfully, after confronting them, they refunded the full amount. That itself speaks volumes.

⚠️ My Advice to Others:

Always ask for a full diagnostic report and video proof of the issue.

Don't accept vague answers like “trust us” when your hard-earned money and laptop’s life are at stake.

Ensure the workspace is professional, clean, and ESD-safe—we have no idea what happens behind closed doors.
